span.p: I need to change the database

div.style: color: rgb(74, 58, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
There is no Flyway and no Liquibase here.
No db/migration folder, no .sql files, nothing records what ran.
Only two mechanisms: Hibernate ddl-auto=update,
and 15 initializer beans on ApplicationReadyEvent

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What kind of change is it?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Add the field with an explicit @Column name and a
deliberate length or columnDefinition — update never widens it later

div.style: color: rgb(30, 58, 41) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
ddl-auto=update handles it at the next boot.
Watch the create table or alter table statement go by —
show-sql is on, that log is your only migration record

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Deploy A: add it nullable, then backfill —
UPDATE images SET version = 0 WHERE version IS NULL —
and confirm zero nulls remain

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Deploy B: add nullable = false plus a @ColumnDefault of 0,
then read is_nullable from information_schema.columns

div.style: color: rgb(92, 32, 24) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Hand-written ALTER TABLE against the database.
Nothing in the application will ever do this for you

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
First the column width — update never widens one, so this ALTER is by hand.
The media, category, person, project and physical_media audit action columns
are length = 20; maqam and guest_correction are 30, analytics and user 32:
ALTER TABLE audio_audit_logs ALTER COLUMN action TYPE varchar(40)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Does an initializer already touch
that column's CHECK constraint?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Just restart. Seven are re-synced from values() — maqam, physical_media,
analytics, guest_correction and user audit action, plus users_tbl.role and
physical_media.digitization. Seven are only dropped and never rebuilt —
image, text, video, audio, project, category, person audit action

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Hibernate's original CHECK is still there and stale. Write a re-syncing
initializer, or hand-drop it — read the real name out of pg_constraint
first, exactly as those initializers do:
ALTER TABLE user_warnings DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS user_warnings_severity_check

div.style: color: rgb(74, 58, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
An initializer bean handles it on ApplicationReadyEvent.
Idempotent, re-runs every boot. Note it fires AFTER SeedDataLoader

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Expand: keep both fields mapped, then copy with an
information_schema-guarded initializer, exactly like
PhysicalMediaSizeColumnMigrationInitializer does for size to physical_size

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Contract in a later deploy, by hand:
ALTER TABLE physical_media DROP COLUMN size

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Can @Index express it —
a plain list of columns?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Declare it in @Table(indexes = ...), the way PhysicalMedia does with
idx_pm_code, or GuestCorrection with idx_gc_media over three columns.
update adds it to an existing table too — confirm it in pg_indexes

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Add CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS to an initializer, next to
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm. On a large table build it
CONCURRENTLY outside the app first, so boot-time DDL is a no-op

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Remove every Java and raw-SQL reference, deploy, wait a release,
back the column up, then drop it by hand:
ALTER TABLE physical_media DROP COLUMN sub_type

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Explicit @Table and @Column names. Add its audit table to
AuditLogIndexInitializer.TABLES, write the enum re-sync initializer
up front, and register any new @Cacheable name in CacheConfig
